messages:
mira (Platform): quick FYI — seeing a spike in streaming reconnects from one org that's blowing its burst quota and causing duplicate token billing on resumes. anyone else seeing this pattern?
sam (API): saw the same with partner B yesterday. client reconnects and resumes from a partial token offset, but our current billing treats replayed tokens as new.
jia (Runtime): runtime note: we only keep a short-lived resume_id mapping; we don't persist per-token ack state. without a per-session token-ack map we can't reliably dedupe on reconnects.
mira (Platform): options on the table: 1) tighten burst windows (sliding/leaky bucket) per-key + per-org, 2) accept resumes as continuation when a resume proof matches and avoid rebilling already-acked tokens, 3) rate-limit reconnect frequency and throttle replays.
sam (API): for option 2 we can require a resume_proof: server signs last_acked_position and client presents it when resuming. if signature verifies we can avoid billing already-acked tokens.
kyle (Console): from console side we need metrics: stream_reconnects, resume_attempts, duplicate_token_count, resume_throttled, and an org-level badge/alert when burst-abuse is happening. also show estimated billed_token_delta for reconnects.
jia (Runtime): implementation caveat: durable last_ack storage for many sessions is costly. lighter approach: keep last-N token hashes per-session in memcache with TTL=30s and do soft-dedupe if resume within that window.
mira (Platform): 30s soft-dedupe + resume_proof seems like the sweet spot for flaky clients; long mobile sleeps will still replay but that's rare.
sam (API): also propose server-side enforcement rule: if resume_attempts_for_session in last 60s > 5 then respond 429 + Retry-After and emit resume_throttled to telemetry to avoid tight reconnect loops.
jia (Runtime): pseudo logic to implement:
```
if resume_attempts_for_session.last(60s) > 5:
  respond 429 Retry-After: 30
  emit event resume_throttled
else:
  allow resume, dedupe via memcache window
```

kyle (Console): UX question: when we mark duplicates as unbilled we should still surface an annotated timeline for the customer: request tags like resume=short-window vs resume=stale-replay, and show which tokens were billed vs deduped.
mira (Platform): + audit log entries for any dedupe/billing decisions so support can explain charges.
sam (API): also add resume-accept response to include a small checksum of last_emitted_token_range so client and server can confirm the reattach point.
opsbot: incident note — org=acme-corp triggered rate_limit_burst twice in last 6h. view: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/requests?filter=stream_reconnects :eyes:
deploy-bot: applied rate limit rule "resume-throttle-v1" to staging at 2026-02-11T14:12:03Z
mira (Platform): action items: sam: spec resume_token header + server behavior (dedupe, 429 thresholds) by EOD tomorrow; jia: prototype memcache dedupe + signature verify in runtime and test with flaky-client sim (due Thu); kyle: small console panel + cost delta estimate with mock data (due Thu); mira: add telemetry metrics above and wire to events.
mira (Platform): TL;DR — short soft-dedupe window + resume_proof handshake + reconnect throttling + console telemetry should cut duplicate billing and provide clear visibility for customers and support. :thumbsup:
sam (API): +1
jia (Runtime): +1
kyle (Console): +1
